titles.to: The X-Ray on the Kitchen Table
The Fox on the Hunting Slope

replace.find: “The village council paid for a month. Not for winter.”
replace.with: “The village council is paying you until the festival. February.” A pause. “They are optimistic.”

replace.find: “October first,” she said. “Thirty days to festival assessment. That is the contract.”
replace.with: “October to February,” she said. “Keep her alive and flying for the festival. That is the contract.”

replace.find: She had thirty days. A thin bird,
replace.with: She had until February. A thin bird,

replace.find: “Progress,” he said. “Yesterday she tried to kill you.
replace.with: “Progress,” he said. “Two days ago she tried to kill you.

replace.find:
The test kit for lead was old stock from Almaty, the box corners soft. She ran it twice because her hands wanted to shake and she would not let them.

Two pink lines. Both times.
replace.with:
The portable lead analyser was old stock from Almaty, the case corners soft. She ran it twice because her hands wanted to shake and she would not let them.

The number came up high. Far too high. Both times.

replace.find: She tapped the stick. “I can treat it. Chelation. A drug that grabs the metal and lets her pass it. Injections, five days. Then we retest.”
replace.with: She tapped the analyser. “I can treat it. Chelation. A drug that grabs the metal and lets her pass it. Injections twice a day, five days. Then we retest.”

replace.find: “Four point one kilos. Twenty milligrams per kilo. Eighty two.”
replace.with: “Four point one kilos. Thirty-five milligrams per kilo. One hundred forty-three point five.”

replace.find: She gave the injection under the skin of the breast, quick.
replace.with: She gave the injection into the breast muscle, quick.

replace.find: and the blood stick still bloomed pink in the test window. Five days of chelation should have pulled the color back. It had not.
replace.with: and the analyser still read far too high. Five days of chelation should have pulled the number down. It had not.

replace.find: The film crackled. The machine buzzed.
replace.with: The plate clicked into place. The machine buzzed.

replace.find: the small heart stopping under the lamp while she recalculated too late.
replace.with: the night nurse's call at midnight, the bird already seizing by the time she drove back.

replace.find: Opening the crop and the proventriculus to lift the shot.
replace.with: Opening the body wall and the proventriculus, reaching through into the gizzard to lift the shot.

replace.find: She found the crop wall, opened it, worked toward the hard curve she had seen on the screen.
replace.with: She found the proventriculus, opened it, and worked through toward the hard curve of the gizzard she had seen on the screen.

replace.find: She checked the crop line once more and nodded.
replace.with: She checked the incision line once more and nodded.

replace.find: “I walk like a person who cannot ride,” she said. “Which you keep forgetting I told you.”
replace.with: “I walk like a person who prefers her own feet,” she said. “Horses are overrated.”

replace.find: When they left, Madina taped the crown drawing to the fridge. “For strength,” she said.
replace.with: When they left, Madina taped the crown drawing to the fridge. “For strength,” she said. The oldest girl, Aigerim, twelve and serious, stayed behind to ask if she could help with the evening feeds, and would not go until Dilnaz wrote her name on the list.

replace.find: “You said you cannot ride and refuse to admit it,” he said. “Today we solve half of that.”
replace.with: “You have walked past every horse in this village for a month and called it exercise,” he said. “Today we solve that.”

replace.find: They walked the horses to the trough.
replace.with: They walked Konyr to the trough.

replace.find: “The vet there said infection. Gave medicine. The bird died in three days.”
replace.with: “The vet there gave injections and sent them home. The bird died in three days.”

replace.find: “After, another hunter cut him open on a table. Found his stomach full of shot.”
replace.with: “My uncle said the injections killed him. Wrong medicine, wrong dose. A city vet in a hurry.”

replace.find: The trough water settled. Somewhere a dog barked twice.
replace.with: The trough water settled. Somewhere up the slope a gate banged.

replace.find: He rubbed his thumb along a crack in his gauntlet, though he was not wearing it.
replace.with: He rubbed his thumb over the bare knuckles of his left hand, where the gauntlet usually sat.

replace.find: He sang when he mended nets, when he waited for tea to boil.
replace.with: He sang when he mended harness, when he waited for tea to boil.

replace.find: Not because I believe it heals the liver.
replace.with: Not because I believe it heals her blood.

replace.find: She noticed the scar at his chin she had never asked about. He noticed her hand had stopped shaking.
replace.with: She noticed the scar at his chin she had never asked about, and that her own hand had stopped shaking.

replace.find: Inside, the clinic smelled of disinfectant and the sour tang of yesterday's coffee left in a tin cup.
replace.with: Inside, the clinic smelled of disinfectant and cold tea left in a tin cup.

replace.find: ran the lead kit on the folding table while the fridge rattled. The second line darkened fast. "Fresh lead. She found another carcass while we were stuck."
replace.with: ran the lead analyser on the folding table while the fridge rattled. The number climbed past last week's. "Fresh lead. She has eaten from a carcass since the surgery."

replace.find: "Where. We cleared the east ridge."
replace.with: "Where. We cleared the east ridge. I flew her there on Sunday, once. She took one hare."

replace.find: "Someone put out new bait in the storm. Someone who knew we could not watch."
replace.with: "Then it was not a hare she found. Someone put the bait back, where they knew you would fly her."

replace.find: He looked at the eagle, at the test strip.
replace.with: He looked at the eagle, at the analyser.

replace.find: Aigerim picked it up. "It was at the district office. They found it behind a cabinet."
replace.with: Aigerim picked it up and read the note clipped to the front. "From the district office. They found it behind a cabinet."

replace.find: "My father's papers. I asked for Akkanat's file years ago."
replace.with: "My father's papers. After you asked, I wrote to the district again for Akkanat's file."

replace.find: He folded the letter once, carefully, along the old crease. His fingers left damp marks.
replace.with: He folded the letter once, carefully, along the old crease.

replace.find: My student heard the engine climbing to the pass last night."
replace.with: We heard your engine climbing to the pass last night."

replace.find: "Forty thousand tenge for parts," he said. "The council has nine."
replace.with: "Four hundred thousand tenge for parts," he said. "The council has ninety."

replace.find: "I said a student heard an engine. That is not proof, Dilnaz.
replace.with: "I said we heard an engine in a storm. That is not proof, Dilnaz.

replace.find: Bakhytzhan stepped close. His shoulder pressed against her red jacket. He smelled of woodsmoke and horse. Karakoz leaned toward him and gave the low chitter she saved for him alone, then, to Dilnaz's surprise, took a strip of rabbit from the forceps without turning away, tearing and swallowing with her head high.
replace.with: Bakhytzhan stepped close, his arm brushing hers. He smelled of woodsmoke and horse. Karakoz leaned toward him and gave the low chitter she saved for him alone, then took a strip of rabbit from his bare fingers, tearing and swallowing with her head high.

replace.find: "She ate from my hand," Dilnaz said. She did not move her fingers from where the eagle's beak had brushed them. "While you watched."
replace.with: "Standing up," Dilnaz said. She had not noticed she was gripping his sleeve until she let it go. "With her head high."

replace.find: Thirty children sat shoulder to shoulder in hats and gloves,
replace.with: Twelve children sat shoulder to shoulder in hats and gloves,

replace.find: Aigerim stood up, important in a yellow scarf.
replace.with: Aigerim stood up, important in a knitted green hat.

replace.find: “That one was old. Frozen hard. I took liver for testing.”
replace.with: “That one was old. Frozen hard. I took muscle for testing.”

replace.find: Aigerim nodded hard, braids bouncing.
replace.with: Aigerim nodded hard, her green hat slipping over one eye.

replace.find: Bakhytzhan stood holding Konyr's bridle. His beard was frosted at the edges. He did not look happy.
replace.with: Bakhytzhan stood holding Konyr's bridle. His beard was frosted at the edges. He did not look happy. The council had called him to the district about the boiler, and Karakoz could not be left alone with Ruslan's truck on the road, so the gorge was hers.

replace.find: Bakhytzhan's hand steadied her elbow for half a second. Warm through three layers.
replace.with: Bakhytzhan's hand braced her knee until she found the other stirrup. Warm through three layers.

replace.find: the sky so blue it hurt to glance up,
replace.with: the sky a hard clean blue,

replace.find: Her eleven crosses from the school blackboard, in the same order, in a round careful hand.
replace.with: Her eleven crosses from the school blackboard, the same dates, in a round careful hand.

replace.find: "Dilnaz-khanum." Ruslan smiled,
replace.with: "Dilnaz-khanym." Ruslan smiled,

replace.find: Tell me what ridge means," she said again,
replace.with: "Tell me what ridge means," she said again,

replace.find: You are a city girl, Dilnaz-khanum.
replace.with: You are a city girl, Dilnaz-khanym.

replace.find: Same dates as the dead foxes we mapped in the school.
replace.with: Same dates as the dead animals we mapped in the school.

replace.find: He kept the book. He gave her a receipt with a stamp.
replace.with:
Before he stamped anything he turned to the back, where the pages went yellow, and read one line aloud from November 2014. Argali, two clients, gut piles left on the east ridge. "Shot in every one," he said. "Lead. That ridge had an eagle hunter then too, yes? Ormanov?"

He kept the book. He gave her a receipt with a stamp.

replace.find: Bakhytzhan went with him, his left arm caught under the stirrup leather.
replace.with: Bakhytzhan went with him, his left hand tangled in the reins.

replace.find: In the hut it smelled of old smoke and dried dung and sheep wool.
replace.with: It was the same hut. It still smelled of old smoke and dried dung and sheep wool, and the skins lay piled where they had left them in December.

replace.find: “No riding like that either. Two weeks at least.”
replace.with: “No riding like that either. Six weeks at least.”

replace.find: Her glasses fogged, then cleared.
replace.with: She took her glasses off and rubbed them on her sleeve.

replace.find: February came with a hard blue sky and wind that lifted dust off the festival field.
replace.with: Festival morning came with a hard blue sky and wind that lifted dust off the festival field.

replace.find: The mare, a bay named Alma, blew warm air into Dilnaz’s gloves. Dilnaz had ridden her every morning for three weeks, first clinging to the saddle, then learning to sit the trot without gripping with her knees.
replace.with: Konyr blew warm air into Dilnaz’s gloves. Dilnaz had ridden the old mare every morning since November, first clinging to the saddle, then learning to sit the trot without gripping with her knees.

replace.find:
“I said I would answer in February.” She adjusted her glasses. “This is February.”

He smiled, just a little. “Then answer after you fly.”
replace.with:
“No to Almaty is not yes to anything.” She adjusted her glasses. “Nobody has asked me the other question here.”

He smiled, just a little. “Then I ask after you fly.”

replace.find: They walked to the field together, leading Alma,
replace.with: They walked to the field together, leading Konyr,

replace.find: He stepped into the circle in his gauntlet, raised his right fist,
replace.with: He stepped into the circle in a borrowed right-hand glove, raised his right fist,

replace.find: Dilnaz mounted Alma with her heart up in her throat.
replace.with: Dilnaz mounted Konyr with her heart up in her throat.

replace.find: She turned Alma, settled her weight,
replace.with: She turned Konyr, settled her weight,

replace.find: Alma shifted but held.
replace.with: Konyr shifted but held.

replace.find: Bakhytzhan was waiting at the rope. His eyes were wet and he did not hide it.
replace.with: Bakhytzhan was waiting at the rope, grinning like one of his students.

replace.find: The poisoned meat pits were filled in. The east ridge was walked clean.
replace.with: The bait sites were cleared. The east ridge was walked clean.

notes: Fixed the contract timeline, the lead test/CaEDTA dose/surgical route, Akkanat's backstory against the 2014 file, the implausible relapse and the 'student heard' engine, the premature feeding from Dilnaz in Ch9, Alma->Konyr and the Almaty answer in Ch15, the children/Aigerim details, 'khanym', the missing quote, and added the 2014 ridge link to Ruslan. Retitled 14 chapters. Left the left-arm carry as the brief specifies (Kazakh berkutchi usually carry on the right) and kept the 'kosh' call.
